questions.question_text: Which is the ascending order of $\frac{1}{2},\frac{3}{8},\frac{3}{4}$?

options.why: This compares numerators without converting one half to eighths.
This reverses the requested ascending order.
This treats fifths as automatically larger without using equivalence.
Three fifths is six tenths, not seven tenths.
Five eighths is greater than one half.
One eighth is less than one quarter.

questions.question_text: What common denominator is most direct for $\frac{2}{3},\frac{5}{6},\frac{1}{2}$?

options.why: Sixths cannot all be rewritten as thirds using whole-number parts.
Twelve works but is not the most direct listed related denominator.

questions.solution_text:
$6$ is a multiple of $2$ and $3$.
The most direct common denominator is $6$.

questions.question_text: If $\frac{n}{12}$ lies strictly between $\frac{1}{2}$ and $\frac{3}{4}$, which value can $n$ have?

options.why: Six twelfths equals the lower endpoint, so it is not strictly between.
Nine twelfths equals the upper endpoint, so it is not strictly between.
Ten twelfths is greater than three quarters.

questions.question_text: Which fraction is third from the left among $\frac{1}{5},\frac{7}{10},\frac{2}{5},\frac{4}{5}$?

options.why: Two fifths is second after converting all values to tenths.
Four fifths is the greatest and lies farthest right.
